title: File Size as a Potential Dataset Bias in Audio-Visual Deepfake Data
abstract: arXiv:2611.32979v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Deepfake detection benchmarks are commonly designed to evaluate whether models can distinguish authentic from manipulated audiovisual content. However, benchmark construction pipelines may introduce unintended associations between class labels and simple file-level properties. In this work, we identify a potential file-size bias in two widely used audio-visual deepfake datasets. In the 1M-Deepfakes Detection Challenge dataset, a score derived from file size alone achieves 70.13% AUC on the validation set. When file size is considered together with video duration, simple file-level methods exceed 90% AUC on 1M and 85% AUC on FakeAVCeleb. Although the same pattern is not observed in DFDC, the results suggest that the observed association is dataset-dependent rather than an inherent property of deepfake videos. translated_title: 文件大小作为视听深度伪造数据中潜在的数据集偏差
translated_abstract: 深度伪造检测基准通常旨在评估模型能否区分真实与被篡改的视听内容。然而，基准构建流程可能会在类别标签与简单的文件级属性之间引入非预期的关联。在这项工作中，我们在两个广泛使用的视听深度伪造数据集中识别出一种潜在的文件大小偏差。在1M-Deepfakes Detection Challenge数据集中，仅基于文件大小得出的评分在验证集上即可达到70.13%的AUC。当将文件大小与视频时长结合考虑时，简单的文件级方法在1M数据集上的AUC超过90%，在FakeAVCeleb数据集上超过85%。尽管在DFDC数据集中未观察到相同的模式，但结果表明这种关联依赖于具体数据集，而非深度伪造视频的固有属性。我们讨论了几种可能的解释，包括编码方式、压缩、源数据以及篡改流程等方面的差异。
tldr: 该研究揭示了两个主流视听深度伪造数据集中存在文件大小偏差——仅凭文件大小和视频时长等文件级属性即可获得很高的检测AUC，说明深度伪造检测基准可能在类别标签与文件属性之间引入了非预期的关联。
en_tdlr: This study reveals a potential file-size bias in two widely used audio-visual deepfake datasets, where simple file-level properties such as file size and video duration alone can achieve high detection AUC, indicating unintended associations between class labels and file properties in deepfake detection benchmarks.
